system.name: Interactive Tracking (InteractTrack benchmark, IMAT baseline)
system.one_liner: A paradigm where users steer a visual tracker at any time with natural-language commands, with a benchmark, protocol and memory-augmented baseline.

content.variant_note: one real basketball video followed through four timestamped user prompts, with the frames above, the prompts on a timeline and the followed targets below
content.argues: Tracking is not fire-and-forget: a user's prompts can redirect the tracker through state changes, target changes and global retargeting within one video.
content.subject: One basketball sequence with four prompts at frames #1, #68, #100, #177 and what the tracker follows after each.

encoding.color_means: One colour per type of interaction, kept on arcs, target boxes, timeline dots, segment titles and crop outlines: green = initial query, yellow = state change / occlusion handling, red = target change / target switch, blue = local-to-global retargeting.
encoding.line_style_means: dashed coloured arcs = the tracked target jumps between two moments; dark-red arrows = a user prompt lands on the timeline; dashed lines in the crop row = path of one target over time
encoding.shape_means: peach rectangle = user prompt; blue circle avatar = the user; filled dot = moment of a prompt; coloured rectangle = tracker box on the target
encoding.marker_means: #n is the frame index at which a prompt arrives
encoding.emphasis: Colour carries the story: each coloured arc names the kind of change and the same colour reappears in the dot and crop segment below.

lessons.what_to_learn: Show an interaction over time as aligned bands: video frames with coloured target boxes, the user's prompts dropped as coloured dots on a timeline, and the resulting target crops. Keep one colour per interaction type through all three bands so the reader sees which prompt caused which change.
lessons.suits: Sequential or interactive tasks on video, dialogue or agent traces where user inputs arrive at different moments and each triggers a different kind of behaviour change.

evidence: User prompts guide the tracker through state changes, target changes, and global retargeting
Initially, the tracker follows the player holding the ball; as the play unfolds, the viewer’s attention naturally shifts

summary: Interactive Tracking is a paradigm in which a user steers a visual tracker at any moment with natural-language commands; the paper adds the InteractTrack benchmark, an evaluation protocol and the IMAT memory-augmented baseline. Figure 1 walks through one basketball video. Four frames (#1, #68, #100, #177) carry coloured target boxes and are linked by dashed arcs named State Change, Target Change and Target Change (local to global). Below, a user avatar with a prompt box ("Who is holding the ball?", "Track it.") drops a red arrow onto a coloured dot on a timeline, and a bottom row of target crops under Query, Occlusion Handling, Target Switch and Retarget shows what the tracker follows after each prompt. One colour per interaction type ties the three bands together.
summary_zh: 交互式跟踪让用户随时用自然语言指令纠正跟踪器。图 1 以一段篮球视频为例：上排四帧带彩色目标框，虚线弧标出状态变化与目标变化；中排用户头像加提示框落在时间轴彩点上；下排按查询、遮挡处理、目标切换、重定向四段展示跟踪裁剪图，同色贯穿三层。
notes: Prior labels kept (worked-walkthrough, actor-interaction); the tracker is not drawn, so actor-interaction is weaker (only the user actor appears). The crop count (13) and avatar count (4) come from the digest's picture sizes. The meaning of the unlabelled salmon arrow and of the small red markers on the ball crop is not stated in the paper text provided.
